text: Cái bug này khó chịu thật, mình tìm cả buổi sáng mà chưa ra.
sample: This bug is driving me crazy — I've been digging into it all morning and still nothing.
note: “Driving me crazy” is the natural way to vent about something annoying.

text: Hóa ra vấn đề là do config sai chứ không phải code.
sample: It turns out the problem was a misconfig, not the code itself.
note: “It turns out” is the go-to opener for surprises.

text: The deploy failed at 5pm on Friday. Tell the team channel.
sample: Heads up — the deploy just failed. Looking into it now, will post updates here.
note: “Heads up” opens almost every alert message.

text: You disagree with a senior engineer’s approach in a code review. Push back politely.
sample: I might be missing something, but wouldn't this break if the list is empty?
chunk: I might be missing something, but...
note: The most powerful disagreement opener in English.

text: Your standup update: yesterday a bug fix, today a new task, no blockers.
sample: Quick one from me — wrapped up the login bug yesterday, picking up the export task today. No blockers.
note: Standup verbs: wrap up, pick up, look into, follow up.

text: Đáng lẽ mình nên review kỹ hơn trước khi merge.
sample: I should have reviewed it more carefully before merging.

text: Tính năng này nghe thì đơn giản nhưng làm thì phức tạp lắm.
sample: This feature sounds simple, but it's a lot trickier than it looks.

text: A recruiter asks: “Tell me about yourself” — give the 15-second version.
sample: I'm a developer based in Hanoi, mostly backend — I like taking messy systems and making them boring and reliable.

text: Cái này không gấp đâu, lúc nào rảnh thì làm.
sample: No rush on this — whenever you get a chance.

text: Your PM asks why the feature is taking longer than estimated.
sample: Honestly, it turned out messier than expected — the legacy code touches way more places than we thought.
note: “X than expected” saves you from word-by-word explanations.

text: Mình định nghỉ sớm hôm nay vì hơi mệt.
sample: I'm thinking of heading out early today — feeling a bit off.
note: “A bit off” covers tired, sick-ish, weird — all of it.

text: Dạo này mình toàn ngủ muộn, sáng dậy không nổi.
sample: I've been staying up way too late lately — mornings are a struggle.
note: “X is a struggle” — instant natural complaint.

text: Trời này mà được nằm nhà xem phim thì thích phải biết.
sample: Weather like this, I'd kill to just stay home and binge something.
note: “I’d kill to / I’d love to” = thích phải biết.

text: Your food delivery is 40 minutes late. Message the shipper without being rude.
sample: Hey, just checking in — any idea how far out you are? No worries if you're stuck in traffic.

text: Mình đang cố cắt giảm cà phê mà khó quá.
sample: I'm trying to cut back on coffee, but it's not going great.
note: Cut back on coffee, spending, screen time — endlessly reusable.

text: Explain to a foreign friend why crossing the street in Hanoi is an art form.
sample: The trick is to walk slowly and never stop — the bikes flow around you like water. Hesitate and you're done.
note: “The trick is to” opens any how-to explanation.

text: Cuối tuần này chắc mình ở nhà dọn dẹp với giặt giũ thôi.
sample: This weekend's probably just chores — cleaning, laundry, the usual.
note: Two words that end a sentence perfectly.

text: Mình quen làm việc buổi sáng hơn, đầu óc tỉnh táo hơn.
sample: I'm more of a morning person — my brain just works better before lunch.
note: “A tea person”, “a dog person” — endlessly reusable.

text: Your gym buddy asks why you skipped this week.
sample: Yeah, I fell off the wagon a bit — this week got away from me. Back on Monday, promise.
chunk: this week got away from me
note: The most forgiving excuse in English.

text: Để mai tính đi, giờ muộn rồi.
sample: Let's deal with it tomorrow — it's getting late.
note: “Deal with” = xử lý, giải quyết, tính. One verb, many jobs.

text: Small talk: a coworker asks how your weekend was. It was boring.
sample: Pretty quiet, honestly — just caught up on sleep and watched stuff. Needed it though.
note: You don’t need an exciting weekend, just a natural-sounding one.

text: Recommend your favorite phở place to a foreign coworker visiting Hanoi.
sample: You've got to try this place near my office — best broth in the Old Quarter, hands down.

text: Decline a friend’s invitation to go out tonight — you just don’t feel like it.
sample: I'm gonna pass tonight — not really feeling it. Rain check?
note: One word-pair that means “lần khác nhé” without guilt.

text: Lâu lắm rồi không gặp, dạo này thế nào?
sample: Hey, it's been ages! How've you been?
note: Greeting chunk. Fires automatically once memorized.

text: Someone compliments your English. Respond without the awkward deny-everything reflex.
sample: Ah, thanks — still a work in progress, but I'm getting there.
note: Accepts the compliment AND stays humble. Perfect.

text: Thôi để mình trả tiền lần này, lần sau bạn mời.
sample: This one's on me — you can get the next one.

text: You forgot a person’s name two minutes after they introduced themselves. Recover.
sample: I'm so sorry, your name slipped my mind — I'm terrible with names the first time.
note: “Slipped my mind” works for names, deadlines, birthdays...

text: Nghe hấp dẫn đấy, kể thêm đi.
sample: Ooh, that sounds interesting — tell me more.
note: The two most powerful small-talk words. People love talking.

text: End a conversation politely because you need to leave.
sample: Anyway, I should get going — it was really good catching up!
note: The universal polite exit. “Anyway” signals the landing.

text: Mình không phản đối, nhưng mình nghĩ nên cân nhắc thêm rủi ro.
sample: I'm not against it — I just think we should weigh the risks a bit more.
chunk: I'm not against it, I just...
note: Disagreement without conflict. Gold in any debate.

text: Càng nghĩ càng thấy giải pháp này không ổn.
sample: The more I think about it, the more this feels wrong.
note: A pattern chunk — memorize the shape, swap the words.

text: Hot take time: is AI going to replace developers? Honest opinion, 2 sentences.
sample: Honestly, I think it replaces tasks, not developers — the job just shifts up a level. The people in trouble are the ones who refuse to use it.
note: “Honestly” buys you a second to think AND sounds confident.

text: Theo mình thì tiền không mua được hạnh phúc, nhưng thiếu tiền thì chắc chắn khổ.
sample: The way I see it, money can't buy happiness — but not having it definitely buys misery.
note: Opinion opener that sounds thoughtful, not aggressive.

text: A friend says remote work is dead. You disagree. Argue back, friendly.
sample: I don't know, man — companies keep saying that, but every good dev I know still gets remote offers.
note: Casual disagreement starts soft, then lands the punch.

text: Cũng tùy thôi, mỗi người một kiểu mà.
sample: It really depends — different strokes for different folks.
note: The honest answer to half of all questions.

text: Rank: bánh mì vs phở vs bún chả. Defend your #1 like it matters.
sample: Bún chả, no contest — it's got the smoke, the herbs, the dipping ritual. Phở is comfort, but bún chả is an event.
note: “No contest” = không cần so. Confidence in two words.

text: Nói thật là mình thấy phim đó hơi bị đánh giá quá cao.
sample: Honestly? I think that movie is kind of overrated.
note: “Kind of” softens any spicy opinion just enough.

text: Tell the story of the worst bug you ever shipped — 3 sentences, make it dramatic.
sample: So picture this: Friday night, everyone's gone home, and I push one tiny fix. Turns out that tiny fix logged every user out of the entire app. I spent the weekend pretending my phone was broken.
note: “Picture this” makes any story instantly cinematic.

text: Suýt nữa thì mình xóa nhầm database production.
sample: I almost dropped the production database by accident.
note: No “suýt nữa thì” gymnastics — just “almost did”.

text: Describe your first day at your current job — one funny or awkward detail.
sample: My first day, I spent twenty minutes looking for the meeting room before realizing it was the glass box I'd been standing next to the whole time.
note: “The whole time” is the punchline chunk of English.

text: Đang giữa chừng cuộc họp thì mất điện, thế là cả phòng ngồi cười.
sample: We were right in the middle of the meeting when the power went out — the whole room just burst out laughing.
note: Emotion verbs: burst out laughing, break down crying, light up.

text: Tell a foreigner about a Tết tradition in your family — story, not Wikipedia.
sample: Every year my mom wakes the whole house up at dawn to clean — apparently luck doesn't visit messy homes. We complain every single year, and every single year we do it anyway.
note: Repetition chunk that makes stories feel alive.

text: Lúc đó mình chẳng biết phải làm gì, đành cứ liều thôi.
sample: At that point I had no idea what to do, so I just winged it.
note: “Wing it” = liều / làm đại. Beautiful little verb.

text: You ran into an old classmate unexpectedly. Tell a friend what happened.
sample: You won't believe who I bumped into at the coffee shop — we ended up talking for like an hour, totally out of nowhere.
note: “Bump into” = tình cờ gặp. “Run into” works too.

text: Chuyến đi đó đáng nhớ lắm, có cả trận mưa to nhất mình từng thấy.
sample: That trip was unforgettable — we got caught in the heaviest rain I've ever seen.

text: Thôi kệ đi, không đáng để cãi nhau vì chuyện đó.
sample: Ah, let it go — it's not worth arguing over.
note: “Not worth doing X” covers a hundred Vietnamese sentences.

text: Để mình xem lại rồi báo bạn sau nhé.
sample: Let me double-check and get back to you.
note: One chunk replaces a whole word-by-word sentence.

text: Your teammate asks you to join a call in 5 minutes, but you are mid-debugging.
sample: Can we push it back like 15 minutes? I'm right in the middle of something.

text: Dạo này mình hơi bận nên chưa trả lời tin nhắn được.
sample: Sorry, things have been a bit hectic lately — just catching up on messages now.

text: A teammate keeps interrupting you in meetings. Raise it with them privately, kindly.
sample: Hey, can I flag something small? I sometimes lose my train of thought when I get cut off — mind letting me finish first?
note: Names the problem without blaming. Pure native phrasing.

text: Chỗ này mình chưa chắc lắm, để mình hỏi lại cho chắc.
sample: I'm not 100% on this part — let me confirm before we move forward.
note: Honest uncertainty without sounding lost. Dev gold.

text: You need a deadline extension. Ask your manager without sounding like you slacked off.
sample: The scope grew more than we planned — could I get a couple more days to do it properly rather than rush it?
chunk: do it properly rather than rush it
note: Frames extra time as quality, not delay.

text: Cái này để mình lo, bạn cứ tập trung phần của bạn đi.
sample: I've got this one — you just focus on your side.
note: Three words that take ownership instantly.

text: Đợt này nhiều việc quá, mình hơi đuối rồi.
sample: It's been a lot lately — I'm stretched pretty thin, to be honest.
note: Professional way to say “overloaded” without complaining.

text: Decline extra work politely when your plate is already full.
sample: I'd love to help, but I'm pretty maxed out this sprint — can it wait, or should we find someone else?
note: “Maxed out” = hết công suất. Sets a boundary nicely.

text: Nói chung là chạy được rồi, còn vài chỗ nhỏ cần dọn lại.
sample: Basically it works — just a few rough edges left to clean up.
note: “Rough edges” = chỗ chưa hoàn thiện. Very natural.

text: Sáng nay kẹt xe kinh khủng, mình đứng yên cả hai mươi phút.
sample: Traffic was brutal this morning — I was stuck at a standstill for like twenty minutes.

text: You burned dinner and have to decide what to do. Talk it through out loud.
sample: Well, that's ruined — let's just order in. I'm not cooking twice tonight.
note: “Order in” = gọi đồ ăn về nhà. Two words.

text: Điện thoại mình sắp hết pin rồi, lát nữa mất sóng đừng lo nhé.
sample: My phone's about to die — if I go quiet, that's why.
note: For phones/batteries, “die” is the natural verb.

text: Dạo này mình tập đi ngủ sớm, thấy người khỏe hẳn.
sample: I've been getting to bed earlier lately, and honestly it's made a huge difference.
note: Closes any “I changed X and now Y” story.

text: A neighbor’s dog won’t stop barking at night. Ask them to help, staying friendly.
sample: Hey, no big deal, but I've been having trouble sleeping — any chance we could keep Max in at night?
note: Softest possible way to make a request.

text: Thôi hôm nay tự thưởng cho mình một bữa ngon đi.
sample: You know what, let's treat ourselves to something nice tonight.
note: “Treat yourself” = tự thưởng. Reuse it weekly.

text: You’re trying to cut spending. Talk yourself out of an impulse buy.
sample: Do I actually need this, or do I just want it? ...Yeah, I'll sleep on it.
note: “Sleep on it” = để mai tính. Buys you a decision.

text: Cuối cùng cũng xong việc nhà, giờ mới được ngồi thở.
sample: Finally done with the chores — now I can actually sit down and breathe.
note: “Finally + done with” opens any relief sentence.

text: Congratulate a friend who just got a new job.
sample: That's amazing, congrats! You totally earned it — when do you start?

text: Để mình giới thiệu, đây là Minh, bạn cùng công ty mình.
sample: Oh, let me introduce you — this is Minh, I work with him.
note: The clean way to bridge two people. Memorize whole.

text: Hôm nay vui quá, lần sau làm tiếp nhé!
sample: Today was so much fun — we've got to do this again soon!
chunk: we've got to do this again
note: The standard warm goodbye. Fires on autopilot.

text: A friend is venting about a bad day. Respond supportively without fixing it.
sample: Ugh, that sounds rough — I'm sorry. You want to talk about it, or just vent?
note: Validates first. Don’t jump to solutions.

text: Bạn ăn thử miếng này đi, ngon lắm, mình bao!
sample: Here, you've got to try this — it's so good. On me, don't worry.

text: Lâu rồi không tụ tập, cuối tuần này cà phê không?
sample: It's been forever — you free for a coffee this weekend?
note: Casual invite shape. Swap coffee for anything.

text: You disagree with a friend’s plan but don’t want a fight. Soften it.
sample: Hmm, I see where you're coming from, but I'm not sure it'll work — can I throw out another idea?
chunk: I see where you're coming from
note: Acknowledges them before you push back. Disarming.

text: Không sao đâu, ai mà chẳng có lúc như vậy.
sample: Don't worry about it — it happens to the best of us.
chunk: it happens to the best of us
note: Comforts anyone who messed up. Pure warmth.

text: Mình thấy học tiếng Anh quan trọng nhất là dám nói sai.
sample: For me, the biggest thing in learning English is being willing to sound stupid.
note: “Willing to” = dám / sẵn sàng. Endlessly reusable.

text: A friend swears expensive phones aren’t worth it. You half-agree. Nuance it.
sample: I'm with you up to a point — past a certain price you're just paying for the logo, but a good camera does change how much I actually use it.
chunk: I'm with you up to a point
note: Agree-then-qualify. The mark of a thoughtful answer.

text: Is it rude to text during dinner? Give your honest position.
sample: I'll be honest, it bugs me a little — but I get that some people are just on call. Depends on the situation, I guess.
note: Mild annoyance without sounding harsh. Very native.

text: Mình nghĩ tiền tiết kiệm quan trọng, nhưng trải nghiệm cũng đáng tiền.
sample: I think saving matters, but some experiences are worth every penny.
note: “Worth every penny” = đáng đồng tiền. Locks in approval.

text: Someone says AI art isn’t “real” art. Take a side, casually.
sample: Eh, I'm on the fence — the tool doesn't bother me, but I do care who's pointing it and why.
note: “On the fence” = chưa ngả về bên nào. Honest middle ground.

text: Nói thật, mình thấy mạng xã hội lợi bất cập hại.
sample: Honestly, I think social media does more harm than good.
note: Clean verdict phrase. Flip it: “more good than harm”.

text: Defend a slightly embarrassing thing you love (a guilty-pleasure show, snack...).
sample: Look, I know it's trash, but that's exactly why I love it — sometimes you don't want to think, you just want to watch.
note: Owning the take is funnier than hiding it.

text: Mình cho rằng thất bại không sao, miễn là rút được kinh nghiệm.
sample: I'd say failing is fine, as long as you take something away from it.
note: “Take away from” = rút ra. Mature, reflective tone.

text: Is money or passion more important in a job? Pick one and commit.
sample: Passion pays the soul, money pays the rent — but if I had to pick, I'd chase something I don't dread on Monday.
note: Forces a clear stance after the nuance. Confident close.

text: Hồi nhỏ mình từng trốn học đi chơi điện tử, bị mẹ bắt tại trận.
sample: As a kid I once skipped school for the arcade — and my mom caught me red-handed.
note: “Red-handed” = bắt tại trận. Perfect for childhood crimes.

text: Describe a trip that went completely wrong but turned out memorable.
sample: Everything that could go wrong did — missed the bus, lost a bag, got rained on — and yet it's the trip I talk about the most.
chunk: everything that could go wrong did
note: The ultimate travel-disaster opener. Sets up the “and yet”.

text: Mình đợi mãi mới tới lượt, vừa tới quầy thì hết hàng.
sample: I waited forever for my turn, and the second I reached the counter — sold out.
note: “The second I X, Y” = vừa mới X thì Y. Builds comic timing.

text: Tell about a time a stranger did something unexpectedly kind.
sample: I was short on cash at the register, fumbling, and the guy behind me just covered it — wouldn't even let me pay him back. Restored my faith a bit.
note: Warm story-closer. Ties the moment to a feeling.

text: Lần đầu đi phỏng vấn mình run đến mức quên cả tên công ty.
sample: At my first-ever interview I was so nervous I blanked on the company's name.
note: “Blank on” = quên sạch. Better than “forgot suddenly”.

text: Recount the moment you realized you were finally getting good at something.
sample: One day it just clicked — I stopped translating in my head and the words were suddenly there. That's when I knew I'd turned a corner.
note: “Clicked” + “turned a corner” = the breakthrough story combo.

text: Hôm đó mưa to, hai đứa phải trú dưới mái hiên cả tiếng đồng hồ.
sample: It poured that day, so the two of us ended up sheltering under an awning for a solid hour.
note: “A solid hour” = nguyên một tiếng. Adds weight to time.

text: Mình tưởng dễ ăn, ai ngờ làm cả ngày mới xong.
sample: I thought it'd be a piece of cake — turns out it took me all day.
note: “Piece of cake” = dễ ợt. The irony sets up the story.

text: Describe the worst meal you’ve ever had — vividly, in two sentences.
sample: Picture grey noodles in water that had clearly given up. I took one bite, smiled politely, and quietly planned my escape.

text: Mình cần thêm chút thời gian để review cái PR này cho kỹ.
sample: I'll need a bit more time to give this PR a proper review.
note: “Give it a proper X” = do X thoroughly, not rushed.

text: Task này phụ thuộc vào team backend nên mình đang bị kẹt.
sample: I'm blocked on this — it depends on the backend team.
note: “Blocked on X” is standup gold for dependencies.

text: Để mình ghi nhanh vào ticket cho khỏi quên.
sample: Let me jot that down in the ticket so it doesn't slip.

text: Hình như lỗi này lọt vào do merge nhầm branch.
sample: I think this bug crept in from a bad merge.

text: Mình đẩy lên staging trước rồi test cho chắc.
sample: I'll push it to staging first and test it just to be safe.

text: Đợt này việc nhiều quá, mình hơi đuối.
sample: It's been full-on lately — I'm a bit swamped.

text: Mình nghĩ estimate này hơi lạc quan.
sample: I think this estimate is a little optimistic.

text: Your teammate's PR has a bug but they clearly worked hard. Point it out kindly.
sample: Really solid work overall — one thing: I think it breaks when the input is null.
note: Lead with praise, then “one thing” softens the catch.

text: You're going to miss a deadline. Tell your manager early and honestly.
sample: Heads up — I don't think I'll hit Friday. I'd rather flag it now than surprise you later.
note: Owning a slip early builds trust.

text: Ask a senior dev for help without sounding helpless.
sample: Got a sec? I've been poking at this for an hour and want a second pair of eyes.
note: Frames help as a sanity check, not a rescue.

text: Explain why you chose a simpler solution over a fancy one.
sample: I went with the boring option on purpose — easier to maintain and it does the job.

text: Give a one-line intro before demoing a feature you built.
sample: So here's the gist: you click here, it auto-fills the rest. Let me walk you through it.

text: A new teammate asks where to start. Point them in the right direction.
sample: Best first step? Get the project running locally — ping me if anything breaks.

text: Sáng nay kẹt xe kinh khủng, mình tới trễ.
sample: Traffic was brutal this morning — I'm running late.

text: Mình ăn gì cũng được, bạn chọn đi.
sample: I'm easy — you pick.
note: “I'm easy” = I don't mind either way.

text: Cuối tuần mình chẳng làm gì, chỉ ở nhà nghỉ.
sample: I did nothing all weekend — just chilled at home.

text: Dạo này mình tập gym đều hơn rồi.
sample: I've been hitting the gym more regularly lately.

text: Cà phê ở đây ngon mà hơi đắt.
sample: The coffee here's great, just a bit pricey.

text: Mình định đặt đồ ăn về, lười nấu quá.
sample: I'm gonna order in — too lazy to cook.

text: Trời nóng quá, mình chỉ muốn ngồi phòng máy lạnh cả ngày.
sample: It's so hot I just want to stay in the AC all day.

text: Your wifi keeps dropping during a call. React naturally.
sample: Sorry, you're cutting out — can you say that again?
note: The go-to phrase for a bad connection.

text: Politely ask a roommate to keep it down at night.
sample: Hey, no rush, but could you keep it down a little? Trying to sleep.

text: You're at a food stall and want it less spicy.
sample: Could you make it less spicy for me? I'm a bit of a lightweight with chili.

text: Reschedule a meetup because you're exhausted.
sample: Mind if we push it to tomorrow? I'm running on empty today.

text: Lâu rồi không gặp, trông bạn khác quá!
sample: Long time no see — you look so different!

text: Để mình giới thiệu, đây là đồng nghiệp của mình.
sample: Let me introduce you — this is my coworker.

text: Hôm nào rảnh đi cà phê nhé!
sample: Let's grab a coffee sometime!

text: Mình phải đi đây, hẹn gặp lại nha!
sample: I've gotta run — catch you later!

text: Cảm ơn nha, bạn cứu mình một bàn thua.
sample: Thanks a ton — you really saved me there.

text: Congratulate a friend who just landed a new job.
sample: That's huge, congrats! You totally earned it.

text: You forgot someone's name at a party. Recover gracefully.
sample: I'm so sorry — remind me your name? I'm terrible with names.

text: Turn down a party invite without offending.
sample: Ah, I'd love to but I'm wiped tonight — next time for sure?

text: Make small talk with a coworker in the elevator.
sample: Surviving the week? Almost Friday at least.

text: Comfort a friend who's stressed about work.
sample: Hey, go easy on yourself — you're doing more than you think.

text: Mình nghĩ cứ thử trước rồi tính sau.
sample: I say we just try it and figure it out as we go.
chunk: figure it out as we go

text: Nói thật thì mình không thích cách làm đó lắm.
sample: To be honest, I'm not a big fan of that approach.

text: Lương quan trọng, nhưng với mình môi trường còn quan trọng hơn.
sample: Pay matters, but for me the team matters even more.

sample: My flight's been delayed two hours.
note: Passive + duration. No “they delayed my flight” — the flight is the subject.

text: Cho mình hỏi ra cổng B12 đi lối nào ạ?
sample: Sorry, how do I get to gate B12?
note: The one direction-asking frame you need. Works for gates, exits, streets, anything.

text: Mình bị lỡ chuyến nối rồi.
sample: I missed my connection.
note: “Connection” alone means the connecting flight. Don’t say “connecting plane”.

text: Vali mình không thấy ra băng chuyền.
sample: My bag didn't make it.
note: Airline speak for luggage that stayed behind. Also used for people who couldn’t come.

text: Mình muốn đổi sang chuyến sớm hơn.
sample: I'd like to switch to an earlier flight.
note: Switch = change between two options. Works for flights, seats, dates, slots.

text: Cho mình gửi hành lý ở đây một lúc được không?
sample: Can I leave my bags here for a bit?
note: “For a bit” makes it sound temporary and reasonable.

text: Khách sạn có cho nhận phòng sớm không ạ?
sample: Is early check-in possible?
note: Hotel vocabulary: check-in, checkout, late checkout — all hyphenated as nouns.

text: Phòng mình ồn quá, đổi phòng được không?
sample: The room's pretty noisy — any chance I could move?
note: The politest way to ask for a favour. Softens a complaint into a request.

text: Đi tới đó mất bao lâu?
sample: How long does it take to get there?
chunk: how long does it take to ___
note: “Take” is the verb for duration. Not “how long do I go”.

text: Đi bộ được không hay phải bắt xe?
sample: Is it walkable or should I grab a cab?
note: Grab = get casually. Grab a cab, grab a coffee, grab a bite.

text: Mình xuống ở trạm nào ạ?
sample: Which stop do I get off at?
note: Get off a train/bus, get out of a car. Different vehicles, different verbs.

text: Mình đi sai đường rồi.
sample: I've gone the wrong way.
note: More natural than “I am lost” when you know roughly where you are.

text: Cho mình xin cái hoá đơn nhé.
sample: Could I get a receipt?
note: The all-purpose polite request. Restaurants, shops, hotels, anywhere.

text: Giá đó có bao gồm ăn sáng không?
sample: Does that include breakfast?
note: Check what’s bundled before you agree to a price.

text: Mật khẩu wifi là gì ạ?
sample: What's the wifi password?
note: Ask it in the first ten seconds anywhere you’ll sit down.

text: Mình muốn ở thêm một đêm nữa.
sample: I'd like to stay one more night.
note: “One more ___” extends anything: one more night, one more day, one more round.

text: Mấy giờ phải trả phòng ạ?
sample: What time's checkout?
note: Contracted “what time’s” sounds far more native than “what time is”.

text: Chỗ đó có đáng đi không?
sample: Is it worth the trip?
note: Worth + noun or worth + -ing: worth the trip, worth going, worth a look.

text: Mình mới tới hôm qua.
sample: I just got in yesterday.
note: “Got in” = arrived. Native travellers almost never say “I arrived”.

text: Mình ở đây một tuần.
sample: I'm here for a week.
note: Duration answer for border control, hotels and small talk alike.

text: Mình đi du lịch một mình.
sample: I'm travelling solo.
note: Solo sounds deliberate and confident; “alone” can sound sad.

text: Mình vẫn còn lệch múi giờ.
sample: I'm still pretty jet-lagged.
note: Adjective, always hyphenated. The noun is “jet lag”, no hyphen.

text: Chuyến bị huỷ, họ xếp mình sang chuyến mai.
sample: The flight got cancelled and they rebooked me on tomorrow's.
note: Airline vocabulary you’ll need at exactly the worst moment.

text: Mình để quên hộ chiếu ở khách sạn.
sample: I left my passport back at the hotel.
note: “Back at” signals the place you came from. Adds the distance for free.

text: Xe muộn khoảng hai mươi phút.
sample: The bus is running about twenty minutes late.
note: Transport “runs” late, people “are” late. Slot the number straight in.

text: Gần đây có chỗ nào đổi tiền không ạ?
sample: Is there somewhere around here to change money?
note: Vaguer and more natural than “where is the nearest…”.

text: Xin lỗi, mình không biết nhiều tiếng ở đây.
sample: Sorry, I don't speak much Japanese.
note: “Much” is the humble version and usually gets you help instead of a lecture.

text: Cho mình chỗ cạnh cửa sổ nhé.
sample: Could I get a window seat?
note: Window seat / aisle seat. There is no “middle seat” request, for good reason.

text: Vali mình chắc quá cân rồi.
sample: I think my bag's over the limit.
note: Works for weight, budget, time — anything with a cap.

text: Đi taxi từ sân bay vào trung tâm khoảng bao nhiêu?
sample: Roughly how much is a taxi from the airport into town?
note: “Roughly” tells them you want a ballpark, not a commitment.

text: Bay mất bao lâu?
sample: How long's the flight?
note: Contract it. “How long is the flight” is correct but sounds like a textbook.

text: Mình định đi lang thang thôi, không có kế hoạch gì.
sample: I'm just going to wander around — no real plan.
note: Wander = walk with no destination. The whole point of a good trip.

text: Chỗ này đông khách du lịch quá.
sample: This place is crawling with tourists.
note: Vivid and slightly negative. Crawling with tourists, with ants, with cops.

text: You're at the airport and your connecting flight leaves in 25 minutes. Ask staff for the fastest way to the gate.
sample: Sorry — my connection boards in twenty-five minutes, what's the quickest way to B12?
note: Lead with the deadline; it turns a question into a priority.

text: Your hotel room smells of smoke. Ask to change rooms without being aggressive.
sample: Hi — the room smells quite strongly of smoke. Would it be possible to move?
note: The most formal polite request. Reach for it with staff you don’t know.

text: A stranger asks you how to get to the train station and you know the way. Explain it.
sample: Yeah, go straight down here, take the second left, and it's right in front of you — five minutes, tops.
note: “Tops” = at most. Native, casual, and reassuring.

text: Your luggage didn't arrive. Report it at the baggage desk.
sample: Hi, my bag didn't come out — it was checked through from Hanoi. What do I need to do?
chunk: what do I need to do
note: Hands the problem to the person who owns it, without blaming them.

text: Check into a hotel: you have a booking, you want a quiet room, and you need to know about breakfast.
sample: Hi, I've got a booking under Jane. If there's anything away from the road that'd be great — and what time's breakfast?
chunk: if there's anything ___ that'd be great
note: Soft-requests a preference without demanding it.

text: You're on a bus and not sure it goes where you need. Ask the driver.
sample: Sorry, does this one stop near the old quarter?
note: “This one” is how locals refer to the bus they’re standing on.

text: Get in a taxi, tell the driver where you want to go, then ask roughly what it will cost.
sample: Central station, please. Roughly what will that run me?
note: Casual way to ask a price. Slightly street, very natural.

text: Negotiate a late checkout — your flight isn't until 9pm.
sample: My flight's not until nine tonight — is there any way I could keep the room a bit longer?
chunk: is there any way I could ___
note: The strongest polite ask in English. Leaves them room to say yes.

text: You've been overcharged for a tour. Push back politely.
sample: Sorry, I think there's been a mix-up — the site said thirty, and this is forty-five. Could you check?
note: Blames the situation, not the person. Keeps everyone’s face intact.

text: A local asks why you chose their city. Answer in two sentences.
sample: Honestly, a friend wouldn't stop talking about the food. Two days in, I get it.
note: Story-shaped answer. Far better than “because it is beautiful”.

text: You need a pharmacy while abroad. Explain to a stranger what you're looking for.
sample: Sorry, is there a pharmacy near here? I need something for a headache.
note: How you ask for medicine without knowing any drug names.

text: Your flight is cancelled. Ask the desk what your options are and what the airline will cover.
sample: So where does that leave me? Is there anything tonight, and do you cover the hotel if there isn't?
note: Asks for options and responsibility in five words.

text: Someone's sitting in your assigned seat on the train. Sort it out.
sample: Sorry, I think that might be my seat — 14A? Let me double-check my ticket.
note: Triple-hedged. Defuses it before it becomes a confrontation.

text: Recommend your hometown to a tourist — three sentences, make them want to go.
sample: It's not on most people's lists, which is exactly why you should go. Get there early, eat at the market, and don't plan anything else. You'll thank me.
note: Turns a weakness into the selling point. Persuasion in four words.

text: You're at passport control: say why you're visiting and how long you'll stay.
sample: Just a holiday — I'm here for ten days, then flying home from Osaka.
note: “Just” keeps it small and uninteresting, which is what you want here.

text: Mình thấy hơi mệt, chắc nghỉ sớm.
sample: I'm feeling a bit run down — I might call it a day.
note: Run down = worn out and slightly ill. The everyday way to say “not right”.

text: Mình đau đầu từ sáng đến giờ.
sample: I've had a headache since this morning.
note: Present perfect for a symptom that is still going. Not “I had”.

text: Mình bị cảm nhẹ.
sample: I've got a bit of a cold.
note: Downgrades anything: a bit of a cold, a bit of a problem, a bit of a mess.

text: Mình ngủ không đủ.
sample: I didn't get enough sleep.
note: Sleep is uncountable here. Never “enough sleeps”.

text: Mấy hôm nay mình khó ngủ.
sample: I haven't been sleeping well lately.
note: Present perfect continuous for an ongoing stretch. Very high-frequency.

text: Ngồi cả ngày nên lưng mình đau nhức.
sample: My back's killing me from sitting all day.
note: Hyperbole, but completely standard. Back, feet, head, shoulders.

text: Mình cần đi khám cái này.
sample: I should get it looked at.
note: Passive causative. You don’t look — you get it looked at.

text: Chiều nay mình có hẹn bác sĩ.
sample: I've got a doctor's appointment this afternoon.
note: Possessive apostrophe is fixed here. Also dentist’s, optician’s.

text: Mình bị dị ứng hải sản.
sample: I'm allergic to shellfish.
note: Allergic takes “to”, always. Worth memorising before you travel.

text: Thuốc này ngày uống mấy lần ạ?
sample: How many times a day do I take this?
note: You “take” medicine in English — never drink or eat it.

text: Mình đang uống kháng sinh.
sample: I'm on antibiotics.
note: “On” + medication. Same shape as on painkillers, on the pill.

text: Mình hơi sốt.
sample: I've got a bit of a temperature.
note: British English uses “a temperature” to mean a fever. Countable, oddly.

text: Mình đỡ nhiều rồi.
sample: I'm feeling much better, thanks.
note: Add “thanks” and it closes the topic politely.

text: Mình tập gym ba buổi một tuần.
sample: I go to the gym three times a week.
note: Frequency formula: number + times + a + period.

text: Hôm nay tập chân, mai chắc đi không nổi.
sample: I did legs today — I won't be walking tomorrow.
note: Future continuous used as a joke about consequences.

text: Mình bỏ cà phê buổi chiều rồi.
sample: I've cut out afternoon coffee.
note: Cut out = remove entirely. Cut back = reduce. Two different promises.

text: Mình cần vận động nhiều hơn.
sample: I need to be more active.
note: Broader and more natural than “do more exercise”.

text: Nhìn màn hình cả ngày nên mắt mình mỏi.
sample: My eyes are strained from staring at a screen all day.
note: Stare = look fixedly. The exact verb for screen fatigue.

text: Mình hay bị cứng cổ.
sample: I get a stiff neck a lot.
note: Habitual “get” + symptom. Not “I have a stiff neck a lot”.

text: Leo cầu thang thôi mà mình đã hụt hơi.
sample: I'm out of breath just going up the stairs.
note: “Just” marks how little it took. Adds the self-deprecation for free.

text: Mình cố đi mười nghìn bước mỗi ngày.
sample: I try to hit ten thousand steps a day.
note: “Hit” a target or number. Also hit a deadline, hit a goal.

text: Người mình đau nhức khắp cả.
sample: I ache all over.
note: Ache is the verb here. Short, complete sentence — no object needed.

text: Đứng lên nhanh là mình bị chóng mặt.
sample: I get dizzy when I stand up too fast.
note: Get + adjective for a change of state. Get dizzy, get tired, get cold.

text: Mình cứ quên uống nước.
sample: I keep forgetting to drink water.
note: Keep + -ing for a repeated failure. Useful and very honest.

text: Mình stress quá nên ngủ không ngon.
sample: I've been too stressed to sleep properly.
note: Too + adjective + infinitive. The blocked-by-a-state pattern.

text: Mình phải đi khám định kỳ.
sample: I'm due for a check-up.
note: Due for = it is time. Works for haircuts, dentists, pay rises.

text: Mình hắt hơi suốt, chắc dị ứng phấn hoa.
sample: I can't stop sneezing — must be hay fever.
note: “Must be” = my best guess. Deduction without any hedging words.

text: Chân mình bị chuột rút.
sample: I got a cramp in my leg.
note: Cramp is countable in this frame. Add the body part with “in”.

text: Mình bị bong gân mắt cá.
sample: I twisted my ankle.
note: Twisted for ankles and wrists; “sprained” is the medical upgrade.

text: Mình đang ăn ít tinh bột hơn.
sample: I'm cutting back on carbs.
note: Cut back = reduce, cut out = quit entirely. Two different promises.

text: Bác sĩ nói mình cần nghỉ ngơi.
sample: The doctor told me to take it easy.
note: Also a goodbye and a calm-down. Three meanings, one phrase.

text: Describe your symptoms to a doctor: headache for three days, worse in the evenings, no fever.
sample: It's been about three days now — worse in the evenings, and no temperature. Painkillers help for an hour or so.
note: Duration, pattern, then what you tried. The order doctors want.

text: Cancel a gym session with a friend because your back hurts.
sample: Going to have to skip today — my back's playing up again. Rain check?
note: Playing up = acting up, misbehaving. Backs, knees, laptops, kids.

text: A colleague looks awful. Ask if they are okay without prying.
sample: You doing okay? You don't have to say, just checking.
note: Offers care and an exit in the same breath.

text: Tell a pharmacist you need something for a sore throat, and that you are allergic to penicillin.
sample: Have you got anything for a sore throat? Just so you know, I can't take penicillin.
note: Flags critical information without making it a big announcement.

text: Tell your manager you need the afternoon off for a medical appointment, without giving details.
sample: I've got an appointment this afternoon so I'll be offline from two — nothing to worry about.
note: Pre-empts the follow-up question and closes the topic.

text: A friend says they cannot sleep. Give one piece of advice without lecturing.
sample: What worked for me was leaving my phone in the other room. Might be rubbish advice for you, though.
note: Frames advice as your experience, so it can’t sound like an order.

text: Decline a drink because you are on medication.
sample: I'll sit this one out — I'm on antibiotics. Next time, though.
note: Declines once, not forever. Keeps you in the group.

text: Someone asks about your fitness routine. Answer in two sentences.
sample: Nothing clever — gym three times a week and a long walk at the weekend. The walk is the bit I actually enjoy.
note: Undersells the routine, which makes it sound sustainable rather than smug.

text: Reassure your mum on the phone that your cough is nothing serious.
sample: Honestly, it's just a cough — I've been sleeping fine and eating properly. I'll go in if it's still here next week.
note: Gives a condition and a plan, which is what worried people need.

text: Ask a receptionist for the earliest available appointment.
sample: What's the soonest you've got? Any day works, morning if possible.
note: Asks for their best offer instead of proposing times yourself.

text: A friend recommends an extreme diet. Push back gently.
sample: I can see why that works for you — I don't think I'd last a week on it, though.
note: Validates first, declines second. Nobody gets defensive.

text: Describe what a burnout week feels like — three sentences.
sample: You're at your desk for ten hours and somehow nothing gets done. Everything small feels enormous. By Friday I'm not tired, I'm just flat.
note: Corrects an assumption to land a more precise feeling.

text: Ask a trainer at the gym to check your form.
sample: Have you got a second to watch my form on this? I don't want to wreck my back.
chunk: have you got a second to ___
note: The smallest possible ask. Very hard to refuse.

text: Tell a friend you have decided to stop drinking, and why — two sentences.
sample: I've knocked it on the head for a while — my sleep was a mess. Ask me again in three months.
note: Idiom for stopping something. Casual, and skips the whole lecture.

text: Cái này bao nhiêu tiền ạ?
sample: How much is this one?
note: The first sentence to have ready in any shop, anywhere.

text: Đắt quá, giảm chút được không?
sample: That's a bit steep — any chance of a discount?
note: Steep = overpriced. Softer and more British than “too expensive”.

text: Mình chỉ xem thôi, cảm ơn.
sample: I'm just browsing, thanks.
note: Gets a shop assistant to leave you alone, politely.

text: Cái này có size lớn hơn không ạ?
sample: Have you got this in a bigger size?
note: Works for size, colour, another material. Shop workhorse.

text: Mình muốn đổi cái này.
sample: I'd like to exchange this.
note: Exchange = swap for another item. Refund = get money back.

text: Mình muốn trả lại và lấy lại tiền.
sample: I'd like a refund, please.
note: Say the word early — it changes which staff member you get.

text: Mình có giữ hoá đơn đây.
sample: I've still got the receipt.
note: “Still” signals you came prepared. Strengthens any return.

text: Có trả bằng thẻ được không ạ?
sample: Can I pay by card?
note: By card, by bank transfer — but “in cash”. Prepositions differ.

text: Cho mình chia hoá đơn nhé.
sample: Could we split the bill?
note: The restaurant essential. “Go halves” is the casual version.

text: Để mình trả lần này.
sample: I'll get this one.
note: Claims the bill without mentioning money at all. Very natural.

text: Tháng này mình hơi cạn tiền.
sample: I'm a bit short this month.
note: Short = not enough money. Understated and face-saving.

text: Mình đang tiết kiệm để mua nhà.
sample: I'm saving up for a flat.
note: Save up = accumulate over time. The “up” matters.

text: Cái đó ngoài tầm của mình.
sample: That's out of my price range.
note: Blames the price, not your wallet. Ends the conversation cleanly.

text: Mình đã huỷ mấy cái đăng ký không dùng.
sample: I've cancelled a few subscriptions I wasn't using.
note: Past continuous for the habit you ended. Justifies the decision.

text: Tiền nhà tăng từ tháng sau.
sample: The rent's going up next month.
note: Prices go up and come down. Never “increase” in casual speech.

text: Cái này đáng tiền lắm.
sample: It's good value for money.
note: The fixed phrase for worth-the-price. Don’t drop the “for”.

text: Mua hai tặng một đấy.
sample: It's buy one get one free.
note: Fixed offer phrase, often shortened to BOGOF in the UK.

text: Lương mình chưa về.
sample: I haven't been paid yet.
note: Passive: you get paid, the company pays. Almost always passive here.

text: Mình bị trừ phí không rõ lý do.
sample: I've been charged a fee I don't recognise.
note: Bank-speak. Passive keeps it factual rather than accusing.

text: Cuối tháng mình mới rảnh tiền.
sample: I'll have a bit more cash at the end of the month.
note: Vague amounts sound relaxed. Exact numbers sound anxious.

text: Mình cân đối chi tiêu mỗi tháng một lần.
sample: I go through my budget once a month.
note: Go through = review item by item. Budget, inbox, list, notes.

text: Cái đó đắt gấp đôi ở chỗ khác.
sample: It's twice the price everywhere else.
note: Multiplier + noun. Also half the price, three times the size.

text: Mình mua cũ cho rẻ.
sample: I bought it second-hand.
note: Hyphenated before a noun. “Used” is the American default.

text: Phí giao hàng bao nhiêu ạ?
sample: How much is delivery?
note: Uncountable here — never “how much are deliveries”.

text: Mình chuyển khoản cho bạn nhé.
sample: I'll transfer it to you.
note: Bank transfers “go to” people. Simple and unambiguous.

text: Mình nợ bạn hai trăm.
sample: I owe you two hundred.
note: Owe takes two objects. No preposition needed at all.

text: Bạn trả trước rồi mình gửi lại sau nhé.
sample: Can you cover me and I'll sort you out later?
note: Cover = pay temporarily for someone. Extremely common among friends.

text: Đồ này giảm bảy mươi phần trăm.
sample: It's seventy percent off.
note: “Off” is the discount word. Not “reduced by” in speech.

text: Thôi mình không mua nữa.
sample: I think I'll leave it, thanks.
note: The graceful in-shop no. Nobody loses face.

text: Giá này có bao gồm thuế chưa ạ?
sample: Is that price with tax included?
note: Ask before you agree. The answer varies by country.

text: Mình tìm được cái rẻ hơn trên mạng.
sample: I found it cheaper online.
note: Comparative after the object. Also: found it faster, found it easier.

text: Đầu tư thì mình không dám mạo hiểm.
sample: I'm pretty risk-averse when it comes to investing.
note: Narrows a claim to one area. Sounds considered and precise.

text: A market seller quotes you double the normal price. Negotiate without being rude.
sample: Come on — I saw it for half that down the road. Meet me in the middle?
note: Names a fair outcome instead of just rejecting their number.

text: Return a jacket you wore once because a seam split. You have the receipt.
sample: I bought this last week and the seam's already gone. I've got the receipt here — can I get a refund?
note: “Already” carries the whole complaint. No anger required.

text: A friend has owed you money for two months. Ask for it back without damaging the friendship.
sample: Hey, no rush at all — but could you send over that two hundred when you get a chance?
note: Removes urgency from a request that is, in fact, urgent.

text: A colleague suggests an expensive restaurant and you cannot afford it this month. Redirect.
sample: I'm being careful this month — could we do the noodle place instead? Just as good, half the damage.
note: Playful word for cost. Keeps money talk light.

text: You have been charged twice for the same order. Write to customer support in three sentences.
sample: I've been charged twice for order 4471 — once on the 3rd and again on the 4th. The second charge wasn't authorised. Could you refund it and confirm by email?
note: Asks for the action and the proof together. Halves the thread length.

text: Ask your manager for a pay rise. Two sentences, no apologising.
sample: I've taken on the release process and the on-call rota since January. I'd like to talk about bringing my salary in line with that.
note: Frames the rise as a correction, not a favour.

text: A salesperson is pushing an extended warranty you do not want. Decline three times, escalating politely.
sample: No, I'm alright, thanks. Honestly, I'd rather not. I'll take it as it is — thank you though.
chunk: I'll take it as it is
note: Final-sounding without being rude. Ends the pitch.

text: Explain to a friend why you stopped buying coffee out every day.
sample: It was four quid a day, which is eighty a month, which is a flight. Once I did the maths I couldn't unsee it.
note: The number-cascade argument. Persuasive without any preaching.

text: Split a group bill where you drank nothing and two people had cocktails. Raise it fairly.
sample: Shall we just do it by what we had? I only had the food, so it's easier that way.
chunk: shall we just do it by ___
note: Proposes the method, not the grievance. Nobody feels accused.

text: Your landlord raises the rent by fifteen percent. Push back in three sentences.
sample: Fifteen percent is a big jump in one go. I've paid on time for two years and looked after the place — could we land somewhere nearer five? I'd much rather stay than move.
chunk: a big jump in one go
note: Objects to the size, not the principle. Leaves room to settle.

text: Turn down an expensive wedding invitation abroad without mentioning money directly.
sample: I'd absolutely love to, but the timing just doesn't work for me this year. I'll take you out properly when you're back.
note: The universal decline. Nobody ever asks a follow-up question.

text: Teach a ten-year-old the difference between saving and spending in three sentences.
sample: Money you spend is gone, and money you save turns into choices later. The trick isn't earning more, it's noticing where it leaks. Start with one thing you'd rather have in a year.
note: Correction structure. Makes advice sound like insight.

text: Ask for the price of a taxi before getting in, then agree.
sample: How much to the old quarter? ... Yeah, that's fine — let's go.
note: Accept and move. Long agreement sounds like second thoughts.

text: A relative asks how much you earn. Deflect without lying.
sample: Enough to keep the lights on, not enough to be interesting. How's the new job treating you?
note: Answers in shape, not numbers, then hands the question back.

text: Explain to a shop that an online discount code did not apply at checkout.
sample: The code SPRING20 was still live when I ordered but it hasn't come off the total. Could you apply it retroactively?
note: Discounts “come off”. Precise and immediately understood.

text: Mình làm lập trình viên được năm năm rồi.
sample: I've been a developer for about five years now.
note: Present perfect for a job you still hold. Never the past simple.

text: Hiện tại mình đang làm ở một công ty fintech.
sample: I'm at a fintech company at the moment.
note: “At” + company name. Simpler and more native than “working in”.

text: Mình phụ trách phần backend.
sample: I look after the backend.
note: Look after = own and maintain. Warmer than “I am responsible for”.

text: Mình đang tìm việc mới.
sample: I'm looking for something new.
note: Deliberately vague. Signals a search without naming any targets.

text: Mình muốn đổi hướng sang làm sản phẩm.
sample: I'm looking to move into product.
note: Move into = change field. The standard career-change verb.

text: Mình nghỉ việc cũ từ tháng trước.
sample: I left my last job in March.
note: “Left” is neutral. “Quit” sounds dramatic; “was let go” means fired.

text: Mình bị cắt giảm nhân sự.
sample: I was made redundant.
note: British phrasing, and it clearly isn’t your fault. Useful distinction.

text: Mình có phỏng vấn vòng hai tuần sau.
sample: I've got a second-round interview next week.
note: Rounds, stages, final. The vocabulary of every hiring process.

text: Cho mình hỏi quy trình tuyển gồm mấy vòng ạ?
sample: How many stages are there in the process?
note: Ask early. It tells you how much time to commit.

text: Mình quan tâm đến vị trí này vì công ty làm về giáo dục.
sample: What drew me to the role is that you're working in education.
note: Cleft sentence. Sounds prepared without sounding rehearsed.

text: Điểm mạnh của mình là xử lý vấn đề khó.
sample: I'm at my best when something's broken and nobody knows why.
note: Answers “strengths” with a scene instead of an adjective.

text: Điểm yếu của mình là hay nhận quá nhiều việc.
sample: I take on too much — I’m learning to say no earlier.
note: Weakness plus the fix. Never leave the first half alone.

text: Mình mong muốn mức lương khoảng ba mươi.
sample: I'm looking for somewhere around thirty.
note: Gives a range without committing to a number. Keeps room to move.

text: Mức đó hơi thấp so với thị trường.
sample: That's a little under market for this role.
note: Uses data, not feelings. Very hard to argue against.

text: Mình có thể bắt đầu sau hai tuần.
sample: I could start in two weeks.
note: “Could” is softer than “can” and leaves the date negotiable.

text: Mình cần thời gian suy nghĩ về đề nghị này.
sample: Could I have a couple of days to think it over?
note: Buys time without signalling doubt. Completely standard.

text: Mình muốn biết thêm về đội nhóm.
sample: I'd love to hear more about the team.
chunk: I'd love to hear more about ___
note: Turns an interview into a conversation. Interviewers relax.

text: Công ty có hỗ trợ làm việc từ xa không ạ?
sample: What's the setup around remote work?
note: Asks about reality, not policy. You get a much better answer.

text: Mình đã dẫn dắt một nhóm bốn người.
sample: I led a team of four.
note: Past simple for a finished responsibility. “Led”, not “leaded”.

text: Mình học được nhiều nhất từ dự án thất bại đó.
sample: I learnt more from that failed project than anything else.
note: Failure framed as education. Interviewers love this shape.

text: Mình đang muốn học thêm về kiến trúc hệ thống.
sample: I want to get deeper into system design.
note: Shows direction. Better than “I want to learn more”.

text: Mình chưa làm cái đó nhưng học nhanh.
sample: I haven't worked with it directly, but I pick things up quickly.
note: Admits the gap and closes it in the same sentence.

text: Mình được thăng chức lên senior năm ngoái.
sample: I was promoted to senior last year.
note: Passive: you get promoted, they promote you. Passive is the norm.

text: Mình muốn xin nghỉ phép hai tuần.
sample: I'd like to take two weeks off in July.
note: Take time off, take a day off. The “off” is doing the work.

text: Mình muốn nói chuyện về lộ trình phát triển.
sample: I'd like to talk about where I'm heading here.
note: Forward-looking and non-confrontational. Opens a career chat.

text: Công việc hiện tại không còn thử thách nữa.
sample: I've stopped being stretched in this role.
note: Stretched = challenged and growing. Positive way to say bored.

text: Mình muốn cảm ơn vì cơ hội này.
sample: Thanks so much for taking the time today.
note: The standard interview close. Say it and then stop talking.

text: Khi nào mình biết kết quả ạ?
sample: When should I expect to hear back?
note: Hear back = receive a reply. Asking it shows confidence.

text: Mình được nhận rồi!
sample: I got the job!
note: Three words. Don’t over-decorate good news.

text: Mình vừa trượt vòng cuối.
sample: I didn't get it — final round.
note: Plain and dignified. No excuses, no explanation needed.

text: Mình có thể giới thiệu bạn với chị ấy.
sample: I could put you in touch with her.
note: The networking phrase. Offers an introduction, not a promise.

text: Mình theo dõi công việc của anh khá lâu rồi.
sample: I've been following your work for a while.
note: Opens any networking message. Flattering and specific.

text: Mình muốn xin phản hồi để lần sau tốt hơn.
sample: Any feedback you can share would really help.
note: Low-pressure request. Makes it easy for them to say yes.

text: Introduce yourself in an interview in three sentences: what you do, what you are good at, why you are here.
sample: I'm a backend developer — five years, mostly payments. The part I'm best at is untangling systems nobody wants to touch. I'm here because you're doing that at a scale I haven't seen yet.
chunk: the part I'm best at is ___
note: Three beats: role, edge, motive. Never ramble past the third.

text: Answer 'tell me about a time you failed' honestly, in three sentences.
sample: I shipped a migration without a rollback plan and took checkout down for an hour. I fixed it, then wrote the runbook we still use. I've never shipped anything irreversible since.
note: Failure, repair, permanent change. The third sentence is the point.

text: The interviewer asks your salary expectations first, before naming a range. Deflect once, then answer.
sample: What range have you got budgeted for this? ... Then we're in the same area — I'm looking at around thirty-five.
chunk: what range have you got budgeted
note: Asks for their number first. Costs nothing, often gains a lot.

text: You are asked about a two-year gap on your CV. Explain in two sentences.
sample: I took two years out to look after my father. I kept my hand in with freelance work, and I'm fully available now.
note: Fills the gap with continuity. Ends on availability.

text: Negotiate an offer that is ten percent below what you wanted, without threatening to walk.
sample: I'm really keen on this. The one thing standing between us is the number — could you get to thirty-eight? I'd sign today.
chunk: the one thing standing between us is ___
note: Names a single obstacle. Makes saying yes feel like closing.

text: Resign from a job you like, to your manager, in three sentences.
sample: I've accepted an offer elsewhere, so I'm giving my notice today. This isn't about the team — the role is closer to where I want to end up. I'll do whatever makes the handover painless.
note: Decision, reason, handover. In that order, always.

text: Ask a stranger on LinkedIn for twenty minutes of their time.
sample: I've been following your work on payment reliability for a while. I'm moving in that direction and I'd value twenty minutes of your take — happy to work around your calendar.
note: Removes every obstacle to a yes, including scheduling.

text: The interviewer asks why you are leaving your current job. Answer without criticising anyone.
sample: I've learnt a lot there, but the problems have stopped getting harder. I'm after something that stretches me again.
chunk: the problems have stopped getting harder
note: Diplomatic truth. Frames the move as growth, not escape.

text: You are asked a technical question you cannot answer. Handle it in two sentences.
sample: I don't know that one off the top of my head. Here's how I'd find out, though — and here's what I'd guess, if you want the reasoning.
note: Admits the gap, then demonstrates the thinking anyway.

text: Turn down a job offer you have decided against, keeping the relationship warm.
sample: I've decided to go another way, and I wanted to tell you properly rather than by email template. I'd genuinely like to stay in touch — this was the closest call I've had.
note: Soft, final, and flattering. They will answer your next message.

text: Ask your manager for a promotion, citing evidence, in three sentences.
sample: Since January I've owned the release process, mentored two juniors and cut our incident count by half. That's the scope of a senior role. I'd like us to make the title match it.
note: Puts the work first and the ask last. Very hard to refuse.

text: Explain a career change from teaching to software in three sentences.
sample: I taught maths for six years, which is mostly debugging other people's reasoning. I started automating my own marking and never stopped. Now I do it full-time, and the explaining part still comes in useful.
note: Reframes the old job as relevant. Turns a risk into an asset.

text: Follow up on an interview after a week of silence, without sounding desperate.
sample: Just following up on last Tuesday — still very interested, and happy to answer anything else. If the timeline has shifted, no problem at all, I'd just like to know where things stand.
note: Asks for a status, not a decision. Easy for them to reply to.

text: Answer: where do you see yourself in five years? Two sentences, no clichés.
sample: Doing the hardest technical work in the room, and being the reason two or three other people are better at it. Whether that has a manager title on it, I genuinely don't mind.
chunk: whether that has ___, I don't mind
note: Commits to substance, stays flexible on form. Sounds mature.

text: Mình không đồng ý với cách làm này.
sample: I'm not sure I agree with that approach.
note: Hedged disagreement. Says no while leaving everyone room.

text: Mình hiểu ý bạn, nhưng mình thấy khác.
sample: I see what you mean, but I see it differently.
note: Acknowledge, then diverge. The safest disagreement shape there is.

text: Cái này mình phải nói thẳng.
sample: I'll be straight with you.
note: Warns them that honesty is coming. Softens the blow in advance.

text: Mình nghĩ bạn hiểu sai ý mình rồi.
sample: I think that came across differently to how I meant it.
note: Blames the delivery, not the listener. Defuses instantly.

text: Bạn nói vậy mình thấy hơi tổn thương.
sample: That stung a bit, to be honest.
note: Names the hurt lightly. Harder to dismiss than an accusation.

text: Mình không nhận thêm việc nữa được.
sample: I can't take anything else on right now.
note: Take on = accept work. Full and final without being rude.

text: Mình cần bạn tôn trọng thời gian của mình.
sample: I need you to respect my time on this.
note: Direct request with a subject. The core boundary sentence.

text: Mình xin lỗi, mình sai.
sample: I got that wrong — sorry.
note: Owns it in four words. Faster and stronger than a long apology.

text: Mình không muốn tranh luận chuyện này nữa.
sample: I'd rather leave this one here.
note: Ends a topic without declaring a winner. Very useful.

text: Nói chuyện này sau nhé, giờ mình đang nóng.
sample: Can we come back to this? I'm a bit wound up.
note: Wound up = agitated. Admitting it lowers the temperature.

text: Cho mình nói hết đã.
sample: Let me finish, then it’s yours.
note: Claims the floor and promises to give it back.

text: Mình đã nói chuyện này ba lần rồi.
sample: This is the third time we've had this conversation.
note: Counting is the most powerful move in any complaint.

text: Mình thấy không công bằng.
sample: That doesn't feel fair to me.
note: “Feel” makes it your perception. Almost impossible to argue with.

text: Mình không thoải mái với chuyện đó.
sample: I'm not comfortable with that.
note: The professional red line. No justification required.

text: Mình cần bạn xin lỗi vì chuyện đó.
sample: I'd like an apology for that, honestly.
note: Asks for repair explicitly. Rare, and very effective.

text: Bạn nói vậy là quá lời.
sample: I think that’s going a bit far.
note: Marks an overstep without matching their escalation.

text: Chuyện này không liên quan đến bạn.
sample: With respect, this one isn’t yours to decide.
note: Boundary phrasing. Firm, formal, and hard to dispute.

text: Mình chỉ muốn làm rõ, không phải bắt lỗi.
sample: I'm not having a go — I just want to understand.
note: British for attacking someone. Denying it early prevents defensiveness.

text: Mình nghĩ cả hai đều có phần đúng.
sample: I think we're both half right.
note: Concedes and claims simultaneously. A quick exit from a stalemate.

text: Mình không thích cách bạn nói chuyện với mình.
sample: I don't like being spoken to like that.
note: Passive keeps the focus on the behaviour, not the person.

text: Bạn hứa rồi mà không làm.
sample: You said you would, and then it didn’t happen.
note: States the gap between words and reality. No adjectives needed.

text: Mình cần biết lý do thật.
sample: What's the real reason?
note: Five words that end most evasions. Use sparingly.

text: Mình không định làm to chuyện.
sample: I don't want to make a thing of it.
note: Downgrades the conflict while still raising it.

text: Mình nghĩ mình nợ bạn một lời giải thích.
sample: I think I owe you an explanation.
note: Opens a difficult conversation from a position of humility.

text: Mình đã cố hết sức rồi.
sample: I've done what I can with this.
note: Closes your responsibility without conceding fault.

text: Mình từ chối lần này nhé.
sample: I'm going to pass on this one.
note: A no that sounds like a choice, not a refusal.

text: Bạn có thể góp ý nhẹ hơn không?
sample: Could you say that a bit more kindly?
note: Requests a change in tone directly. Surprisingly well received.

text: Mình thấy mình bị gạt ra ngoài.
sample: I felt left out of that decision.
note: Passive feeling + the specific event. Precise, not accusatory.

text: Mình không giận, chỉ là thất vọng.
sample: I'm not angry, just disappointed.
note: Downgrade-and-name. Lands far harder than shouting.

text: Mình cần thời gian bình tĩnh lại.
sample: I need ten minutes to cool off.
note: Names the pause and its purpose. Nobody can refuse it.

text: Mình sẽ không nhắc lại chuyện này nữa.
sample: I won't bring it up again.
note: Bring up = raise a topic. A promise that ends a conflict properly.

text: Mình muốn hoà, không muốn thắng.
sample: I'd rather sort this out than win it.
note: Reframes the whole argument. Often ends it on the spot.

text: A colleague takes credit for your work in a meeting. Address it afterwards in three sentences.
sample: Quick one about the meeting — the migration plan was mine, and it landed as though it was yours. I don't think you meant it that way. Could you flag it in the thread so the record's straight?
note: Names the harm, offers an excuse, requests one specific fix.

text: Your flatmate has left the kitchen a mess for the fourth time. Raise it without a row.
sample: I'm going to sound like your mum, but the kitchen's been like this four days running. What's a system that actually works for you?
note: “Running” = consecutively. The count carries the complaint.

text: Someone jumps the queue in front of you. Say something.
sample: Sorry — I think there's a queue, mate.
note: Hedged, but unmistakable. British conflict in six words.

text: Your manager gives you an unreasonable deadline. Push back with an alternative.
sample: If it has to be Friday, something has to come off the list. I can do the API by Friday or all three by Wednesday — your call.
chunk: something has to come off the list
note: Trades scope for time instead of refusing outright.

text: A friend repeatedly cancels plans last minute. Tell them how it lands.
sample: I'm not cross, but I've stopped making plans around you and I don't like that. Can we only book things you actually want to do?
chunk: I've stopped ___ and I don't like that
note: Reports the consequence, not the crime. Very hard to dismiss.

text: Someone makes a joke at your expense in front of others. Respond in the moment.
sample: Ha — bit close to the bone, that one.
note: Marks the overstep with a smile. Nobody escalates.

text: A client keeps adding work outside the agreed scope. Hold the line in three sentences.
sample: Happy to do it — it's outside what we agreed, so it'd be a change to the estimate. Want me to price it up? Otherwise it goes in the next phase.
chunk: want me to price it up?
note: Says yes to the work and no to doing it free.

text: You were wrong in a heated argument yesterday. Apologise properly, in three sentences.
sample: I've had a think, and you were right. I got defensive because I was embarrassed, which isn't your problem. Sorry — I'll do better next time.
note: Explains without excusing. The hallmark of a real apology.

text: A relative makes a remark about your life choices at dinner. Deflect without a scene.
sample: You know what, let's not do this over dinner. Ask me properly another time and I'll tell you the whole thing.
note: Defers rather than refuses. Protects the room and the relationship.

text: Tell a teammate their constant Slack pings are wrecking your focus.
sample: I'm going heads-down between ten and one — I'll miss your pings in that window. Anything urgent, just call me.
note: States the boundary and the escape hatch in one breath. Zero friction.

text: Someone blames you for a production outage that was not your fault. Correct the record calmly.
sample: That deploy wasn't mine — it went out from the release branch on Tuesday. Happy to help fix it, but I'd like that bit clear.
note: Facts, cooperation, then one firm sentence. In that order.

text: A friend asks to borrow money and you want to say no. Refuse in two sentences.
sample: I'm going to say no, and it's nothing to do with you. Lending to mates is the one thing I've learnt not to do.
chunk: it's nothing to do with you
note: Removes the personal sting from a refusal.

text: You are being talked over repeatedly in a video call. Reclaim the floor.
sample: Hang on — I hadn't finished. Thirty seconds and then I'm done.
note: Past perfect asserts a fact. The time limit makes it reasonable.

text: Someone apologises to you but you are not ready to accept it. Respond honestly.
sample: I appreciate you saying that. I'm not quite there yet, but I will be — give me a bit.
note: Refuses to fake forgiveness without rejecting the person.

text: Dạo này mình thấy hơi tuột mood.
sample: I've been a bit flat lately.
note: Flat = low energy, not quite sad. The most useful mood word in English.

text: Mình lo quá không ngủ được.
sample: My head wouldn’t switch off last night.
note: Metaphor for stopping thought. Everyone recognises it instantly.

text: Mình thấy quá tải.
sample: I'm completely swamped.
note: Buried in work. Stronger than busy, shorter than overwhelmed.

text: Mình thấy tội lỗi vì đã không giúp.
sample: I feel bad that I didn’t help.
note: The everyday guilt frame. “Feel guilty” sounds much heavier.

text: Mình hơi chạnh lòng.
sample: It got to me a bit, that.
note: Got to me = affected me emotionally. Understated and very natural.

text: Mình đang cần người nói chuyện.
sample: I could do with a chat, honestly.
note: Softest possible way to ask for support. Almost never refused.

text: Mình thấy nhẹ cả người.
sample: That's a weight off, honestly.
note: Relief after a burden lifts. Fixed metaphor, hugely common.

text: Mình hơi ngợp với mọi thứ.
sample: It's all a bit much at the moment.
note: Overwhelm, stated mildly. Very British, very useful.

text: Mình vui thật sự vì bạn.
sample: I'm genuinely happy for you.
note: “For” not “about”. Happy about a thing, happy for a person.

text: Mình thấy trống rỗng sau khi xong dự án.
sample: I felt a bit empty once it was finished.
note: Post-achievement flatness. Adding “a bit” keeps it conversational.

text: Mình đang cố giữ bình tĩnh.
sample: I'm trying to keep a lid on it.
note: Containing a feeling or situation. Vivid and idiomatic.

text: Mình thất vọng về bản thân.
sample: I'm annoyed at myself, mostly.
note: Self-directed frustration. Lighter and truer than “I hate myself”.

text: Mình cảm thấy không thuộc về nơi này.
sample: I feel like I don’t quite fit in here.
note: “Quite” softens it. The classic expat and new-job feeling.

text: Mình thấy tự hào về mình hôm nay.
sample: I'm quietly proud of that one.
note: Pride without boasting. Almost impossible to dislike.

text: Mình đang bực nhưng không muốn nói ra.
sample: I'm fine — I'm just chewing on something.
note: Admits preoccupation without opening the topic.

text: Mình nhớ nhà.
sample: I'm a bit homesick.
note: One word carries the whole feeling. “A bit” keeps it conversational.

text: Mình thấy cô đơn dù xung quanh đông người.
sample: I can feel lonely in a room full of people.
note: Concrete image beats any abstract explanation.

text: Mình hồi hộp quá.
sample: I've got butterflies.
note: Nervous excitement in the stomach. Positive or neutral, never negative.

text: Mình sợ mình làm không nổi.
sample: I'm scared I'm not up to it.
note: Up to it = capable enough. Very common in self-doubt.

text: Mình cảm ơn bạn thật lòng.
sample: That meant a lot to me.
note: Past tense makes it about a specific act. More sincere than “thank you”.

text: Mình thấy khó chịu mà không rõ vì sao.
sample: I'm out of sorts and I can't tell you why.
note: Slightly off, physically or emotionally. Beautifully vague.

text: Mình đang vui, đừng làm mình tụt mood.
sample: I'm in a good mood — don't ruin it.
note: In a good/bad mood. Always “in”, never “on”.

text: Mình thấy tủi thân.
sample: I felt a bit sorry for myself, if I’m honest.
note: Self-pity, admitted with humour. Disarms any judgement.

text: Mình xúc động khi đọc thư đó.
sample: That letter got me right in the chest.
note: Physical location for an emotional hit. Vivid and modern.

text: Mình chán không muốn làm gì.
sample: I can't be bothered with anything today.
note: The single most British phrase for apathy. Learn it.

text: Mình đỡ hơn khi nói ra.
sample: Saying it out loud helped, actually.
note: Marks the shift from thinking to speaking. Small phrase, big meaning.

text: Mình thấy mình vô dụng.
sample: I feel like I'm not contributing anything.
note: Specific and workplace-safe. Better than a global self-judgement.

text: Mình đang phấn khích quá.
sample: I'm buzzing.
note: High energy and delight. One word, extremely current.

text: Mình thấy tim đập nhanh vì lo.
sample: My heart was going before I even started.
note: Continuous for a racing heart. Idiomatic and physical.

text: Mình không sao, chỉ là mệt.
sample: I'm alright, just tired.
note: The most-used deflection in English. Also sometimes true.

text: Mình thấy tội cho bạn ấy.
sample: I felt for him, honestly.
note: Feel for = sympathise with. No “sorry” required.

text: Mình đang bị cuốn vào suy nghĩ.
sample: I'm overthinking it again.
note: One verb for the whole spiral. Instantly relatable.

text: Mình thấy được an ủi nhiều.
sample: That helped more than you know.
note: Gratitude with a hidden depth. Quietly powerful.

text: Mình cần ở một mình chút.
sample: I just need a bit of space today.

text: A friend messages that their parent has died. Reply in two sentences.
sample: I'm so sorry. I'm not going to fill this with words — tell me what would actually help, or nothing at all, and I'll just be around.
chunk: tell me what would actually help
note: Refuses cliché and offers presence. What people remember.

text: You have been anxious for weeks. Tell a close friend in three sentences.
sample: I've been in a bit of a hole for a few weeks. Nothing's happened, which somehow makes it harder to explain. I'm not after advice, I just wanted one person to know.
note: Sets the terms of the support you want. Prevents unhelpful fixing.

text: A colleague is visibly upset at their desk. Say something in the moment.
sample: Hey — do you want company or space? Either's fine.
note: Offers two options and accepts both. Zero pressure.

text: Congratulate a friend whose success makes you a little jealous. Be honest and warm.
sample: I'm thrilled for you, and mildly sick with envy, which is how you know it's real. Genuinely well done.
chunk: which is how you know it’s real
note: Admits the envy to prove the sincerity. Very charming.

text: Your partner asks what is wrong and you do not know. Answer honestly.
sample: Nothing I can point at. I'm just off today, and I'd rather sit next to you than talk about it.
note: Names the vagueness instead of denying the feeling.

text: Comfort someone who failed an exam, without minimising it.
sample: That's genuinely rubbish, and you're allowed to be gutted about it. It's also not the end of the road — but that's for tomorrow.
note: Permission-giving. Far better than “don’t be sad”.

text: Tell your manager you are close to burning out. Three sentences, professional.
sample: I want to flag something before it becomes a problem: I'm running close to empty. I'd like to look at what comes off my plate for the next month. I'm not asking to drop anything permanently.
note: Frames it as planning, not collapse. Keeps you in control.

text: A friend keeps apologising for being a burden. Reassure them.
sample: You're not a burden, you're a friend having a hard month. Stop apologising — it's the one thing I'll actually get annoyed about.
note: Corrects the self-description with warmth and a joke.

text: Someone asks how you really are, and you decide to tell the truth.
sample: Honestly? Not great. Tired, a bit low, nothing dramatic — but thanks for asking properly.
note: Rewards a real question. Encourages people to ask again.

text: Cheer up a friend who did not get a job they wanted, in three sentences.
sample: You wanted that one, so of course it hurts. You also got to the final round out of two hundred people. Give it two days, then send me your next three.
note: Allows the feeling and sets a gentle deadline.

text: Explain to a friend why you have been quiet for a month.
sample: I went a bit underground — nothing happened, I just didn't have the energy to be good company. I'm back, and I'm sorry for the silence.
note: Explains withdrawal without drama. Easy to forgive.

text: Tell someone you are proud of them, specifically.
sample: I'm proud of you — not for the result, for the fact you did it scared. That's the bit nobody sees.
note: Praises the courage, not the outcome. Lands much deeper.

text: A friend says something that upset you but they clearly did not mean it. Raise it kindly.
sample: I know you didn't mean it like that, and it still sat badly with me. I'd rather tell you than let it go weird.
note: Protects the friendship as the reason for speaking up.

text: You are nervous before something big. Talk yourself through it out loud, three sentences.
sample: Right — I'm nervous, which is just my body taking this seriously. I've done the work, and I don't need it to be perfect. Start talking and the rest follows.
chunk: just my body taking this seriously
note: Reframes fear as readiness. Genuinely calming to say aloud.

text: Cho mình xin phép nói một chút.
sample: Can I jump in here?
note: The standard polite interruption. Short enough to fit any gap.

text: Mình bổ sung thêm một ý nhé.
sample: Just to add to that —
note: Builds on someone instead of competing. Very well received.

text: Mình chưa hiểu rõ ý đó.
sample: Sorry, I'm not quite following.
note: Admits confusion without blaming the speaker.

text: Bạn nói lại phần đó được không?
sample: Could you go over that last bit again?
note: Go over = review. Standard in meetings and lessons alike.

text: Mình muốn quay lại ý trước đó.
sample: Can we go back to what Minh said?
note: Rescues a dropped point. Also makes you look attentive.

text: Mình nghĩ chúng ta đang đi lệch chủ đề.
sample: I think we're drifting a bit.
note: Names the derail gently. Nobody feels blamed.

text: Để mình tóm lại nhé.
sample: So, to sum up —
note: Signals the ending. Buys you the floor for one final minute.

text: Mình sẽ chia sẻ màn hình.
sample: I'll share my screen.
note: The most-used sentence in modern working life.

text: Mọi người nghe rõ mình không?
sample: Can everyone hear me okay?
note: Ask once at the start, never again. Short and standard.

text: Mình bị mất tiếng lúc đó.
sample: Sorry, you cut out for a second.
chunk: you cut out for a second
note: The fixed phrase for dropped audio. Exactly the right verb.

text: Mình sẽ gửi lại phần này sau.
sample: I'll follow up on that after the call.
note: Parks a detail without dropping it. Very professional.

text: Mình xin phép ghi lại ý đó.
sample: Let me note that down.
note: Signals you took it seriously. Small phrase, big effect.

text: Mình chốt lại là thứ Sáu nhé.
sample: So we're agreed: Friday.
note: Closes a decision out loud. Prevents a repeat meeting.

text: Mình hết thời gian rồi.
sample: We're coming up on time.
note: Warns without cutting anyone off. The meeting-chair classic.

text: Mình đồng ý với ý kiến của Hương.
sample: I'm with Huong on this.
note: Backs someone explicitly. Builds alliances fast.

text: Cho mình một phút chuẩn bị.
sample: Give me a second to pull it up.
note: Pull up = open on screen. Standard in demos.

text: Mình sẽ trình bày trong mười phút.
sample: I'll keep this to ten minutes.

text: Trước khi bắt đầu, mình nói nhanh về bối cảnh.
sample: Quick bit of context before I start.
note: Frames the talk. Prevents every early question.

text: Cuối buổi mình sẽ nhận câu hỏi.
sample: I'll take questions at the end.
note: Controls the shape of your own presentation.

text: Câu hỏi hay, để mình trả lời.
sample: Good question — so the short answer is no.
note: Answers before explaining. Respects everyone’s time.

text: Mình chưa có số liệu đó, sẽ kiểm tra lại.
sample: I haven't got that number to hand — I'll check and come back.
note: Admits the gap and commits to a fix. Never bluff a number.

text: Mình muốn nghe ý kiến của mọi người.
sample: What's everyone thinking?
note: Opens the floor without singling anybody out.

text: Bạn nghĩ sao về cái này?
sample: Where do you land on this?
note: Asks for a position, not a monologue. Gets sharper answers.

text: Mình nói hơi dài, xin lỗi.
sample: Sorry, I've talked for too long.
